edges.effect_quant: In a 16-week pediatric trial, oligofructose-enriched inulin improved fullness and lowered prospective food consumption versus placebo in 42 children with overweight or obesity. Smaller adult trials also found lower desire to eat after repeated inulin intake, although a crossover study in 29 adults with type 2 diabetes found no appetite or energy-intake benefit.
edges.population: children with overweight or obesity and adults consuming inulin-type fructans or related prebiotic inulin interventions
edges.mechanism: Inulin may support satiety through colonic fermentation to short-chain fatty acids that feed into appetite signaling and meal termination pathways, especially over repeated exposure rather than after a single dose. The benefit seems more consistent in weight-management settings than in all metabolic contexts, which fits a modest fermentation-driven rather than dramatic anorectic effect.
edges.summary: Inulin supplementation modestly supports satiety, but not in every population. Repeated intake tends to improve fullness and lower desire to eat in children with overweight and in some healthy-adult studies, while a trial in adults with type 2 diabetes found no meaningful appetite effect. The safest conclusion is a small, context-dependent satiety benefit.
edges.caveats: Most trials are small and use subjective appetite scales, with mixed translation into actual energy intake. This edge is better read as a mild supportive tool than as a reliably strong appetite suppressant.

evidence.citation: Nicolucci et al 2017 Am J Clin Nutr
evidence.notes: Prebiotic supplementation improves appetite control in children with overweight and obesity: a randomized controlled trial.

evidence.citation: Meyer et al 2016 Br J Nutr
evidence.notes: Eight-day consumption of inulin added to a yogurt breakfast lowers postprandial appetite ratings but not energy intakes in young healthy females: a randomised controlled trial.

evidence.citation: Guess et al 2021 J Nutr Sci
evidence.notes: Effect of inulin-type fructans on appetite in patients with type 2 diabetes: a randomised controlled crossover trial.
